slides.title: 4 questions that are harder than they look
slides.body:
Great thinkers asked them long ago.
We still can't agree.

slides.title: Would you plug into a machine that gave you a perfect life?
slides.body: Robert Nozick's 'experience machine' could make any life feel completely real. Most people say no. He thought that shows we want to actually do things, not just feel good.
slides.source: Robert Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia, 1974

slides.title: If a teleporter copied you perfectly, would you step in?
slides.body: Derek Parfit imagined a machine that scans you, destroys your body and builds an exact copy, memories and all. Travel, or the end of you? Parfit said thinking about it made him less afraid of death.

slides.title: Could you sit alone in a quiet room?
slides.body: Pascal wrote that all of humanity's problems come from not being able to. In a 2014 study, many people left alone with their thoughts for 6 to 15 minutes chose a mild electric shock instead.
slides.source: Pascal, Pensées · Wilson et al., Science, 2014

slides.title: Is life short, or do we waste it?
slides.body: Seneca argued we don't have too little time: we spend too much of it on things we don't value, as if we'd live forever. What would you do with one extra hour a day?
slides.source: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life

slides.title: Which one is still on your mind?
slides.body: Comment its number and your answer. Save this for a quiet evening.
